questionText: What is the most common connector used on UTP network cable?
explanation: The most common UTP connector is RJ45 (registered jack), a keyed connector. BNC connectors are used on coaxial cable, and SC and ST on fiber-optic cable.

questionText: Which IEEE code refers to the Ethernet wiring standards used for UTP cable?
explanation: UTP is used for the Ethernet wiring standards managed by IEEE and referred to by code 802.3; 802.11 is the committee for wireless LAN standards.

questionText: Which cable type transmits signals as pulses of light?
explanation: Fiber-optic cabling uses glass or plastic fibers to guide light impulses, while twisted-pair and coaxial cables carry electric current on copper conductors.

questionText: Which device converts a computer's digital signals to analog signals for standard telephone lines?
explanation: A modem converts digital signals to analog (modulation) and back (demodulation); its name is a contraction of modulate/demodulate. A transponder belongs to satellites.

questionText: Which wireless technology replaces the cables between nearby devices, such as a phone and a headset?
explanation: Bluetooth is a short-range wireless technology that replaces cables connecting electronic devices, allowing a phone conversation via a headset.

questionText: Which wireless waves does a TV remote control use to change channels?
explanation: Infrared waves have wavelengths longer than visible light, so they are invisible, and you use them to change channels with a TV remote control.

questionText: In a cellular network, what is the fixed transceiver that serves one cell called?
explanation: Each cell contains an antenna and is controlled by a base station (cell site); the mobile station is the moving phone, and earth stations belong to satellite systems.

questionText: Which data transmission mode lets both stations send and receive at the same time, as in a telephone call?
explanation: In full-duplex mode both stations can transmit and receive simultaneously, like a two-way street; the telephone network is the common example.

questionText: In IPv4 dotted decimal notation (x.x.x.x), what values can each x take?
explanation: IPv4 addresses are 32-bit numbers written in dotted decimal as x.x.x.x, where each x can be any value between 0 and 255, as in 192.0.2.146.

questionText: Which committee is responsible for wireless LAN standards marketed under the Wi-Fi brand?
explanation: The IEEE 802.11 committee is responsible for WLAN standards, and most modern WLANs are based on 802.11 and marketed as Wi-Fi.

questionText: Why are the two wires in twisted-pair cable twisted together?
options: So noise hits both wires equally
So it can bend around corners
correctAnswer: So noise hits both wires equally
explanation: Twisting makes it probable that both wires are equally affected by noise or crosstalk, keeping a balance at the receiver; parallel wires would be affected differently.

questionText: Which Ethernet cable type is used to connect a computer to a switch or hub?
explanation: Straight-through cable connects different network devices, such as computers to switches or hubs; crossover cable connects similar devices, such as computer to computer.

questionText: In an environment with electric motors and radio transmitters, which cable is the preferred solution?
explanation: UTP is subject to external electromagnetic interference, so where there are many interference sources such as motors and RF transmitters, shielded twisted-pair may be preferred.

questionText: Which coaxial cable connector family includes T-shaped and terminator variants?
explanation: The most common coaxial connector is the Bayonet Neill-Concelman (BNC) connector, with BNC T and BNC terminator variants; MT-RJ is a fiber connector the size of RJ45.

questionText: How do single mode and multimode fiber compare?
options: Single mode goes farther, at higher cost
Multimode reaches farther and costs more
Single mode has the larger diameter
correctAnswer: Single mode goes farther, at higher cost
explanation: Multimode cable has a larger diameter, and both give high bandwidth at high speed, but single mode provides more distance and is more expensive.

questionText: Which wireless propagation method sends very high-frequency signals in straight lines from antenna to antenna?
explanation: In line-of-sight propagation, very high-frequency signals travel in straight lines between directional antennas; ground propagation hugs the earth and sky propagation reflects off the ionosphere.

questionText: Why are radio waves good for multicasting such as AM and FM radio?
explanation: Radio waves are omnidirectional, propagating in all directions so any receiving antenna can get them, which suits one sender with many receivers. Microwaves are unidirectional.

questionText: Which two antenna types are used for microwave communications?
explanation: Microwaves need unidirectional antennas; the two types used are the parabolic dish and the horn. Omnidirectional antennas are used for radio waves.

questionText: What does a mobile switching center (MSC) do in a cellular network?
options: It connects, records and bills calls
It powers each cell's antenna with solar energy
It sends signals to satellites in orbit
It converts digital signals into analog
correctAnswer: It connects, records and bills calls
explanation: The MSC is a computerized center that coordinates the base stations with the telephone central office and is responsible for connecting calls, recording call information and billing.

questionText: At what altitude is the single orbit for geostationary (GEO) satellites?
explanation: There is only one orbit, at 35,786 km, for GEO satellites; MEO satellites are between 5,000 and 15,000 km and LEO satellites normally below 2,000 km.

questionText: Which data transmission mode is like a one-lane road with traffic allowed in both directions?
explanation: In half-duplex each station can transmit and receive, but not at the same time, like a one-lane road where cars going one way must wait. Full-duplex is a two-way street.

questionText: What is the default network mask for a Class C IP address?
explanation: The default masks are 255.0.0.0 for Class A, 255.255.0.0 for Class B and 255.255.255.0 for Class C, matching their 8, 16 and 24 network bits.

questionText: Which class does the IP address 192.168.1.10 belong to?
explanation: The first octet decides the class: 192 lies in the Class C range 192 to 223. Class B is 128 to 191 and Class D is 224 to 239.

questionText: What are Class D IP addresses used for?
explanation: Classes A, B and C are used for host addresses; Class D is used for multicast and Class E for experimental purposes.

questionText: Why is MEO the orbit chosen between the two Van Allen belts?
options: Charged particles in a belt would destroy it
The belts block all radio waves sent from Earth
The belts make satellites move too slowly
Satellites in the belts cannot see the Earth
correctAnswer: Charged particles in a belt would destroy it
explanation: A Van Allen belt contains charged particles, and a satellite orbiting in one would be destroyed by them; the MEO orbits are located between the two belts.

questionText: Why do digital signals have an advantage over analog signals over long distances?
options: On-off pulses resist noise and can be boosted
Digital signals never need to be strengthened over any distance
Digital signals change their amplitude to carry more information
Analog signals cannot be sent over telephone lines at all
correctAnswer: On-off pulses resist noise and can be boosted
explanation: Digital signals are discrete on-off pulses that are less affected by noise, since it is easier to tell on from off, so they can be repeatedly strengthened over long distances.

questionText: How can a WLAN access point (AP) effectively double the maximum distance between wireless nodes?
options: By lowering the data rate to zero
explanation: The access point can act as a repeater for wireless nodes, effectively doubling the maximum distance between them; larger areas use several APs with 10 to 15% overlap.

questionText: How much overlap is recommended when several access points are installed to cover a large area?
explanation: To service larger areas, multiple access points may be installed with a 10 to 15% overlap so coverage is continuous.

questionText: Which 4G objective applies to stationary users?
explanation: The 4G objectives include 100 Mbit/s for access in a moving car and 1 Gbit/s for stationary users; 11 Mbit/s is the WLAN rate mentioned.

questionText: Why is fiber-optic cable the standard for connecting networks between buildings?
options: It resists electrical noise, moisture and lightning
It is cheaper and easier to install than copper cable
It can be connected with ordinary RJ45 connectors
It carries electric current further than coaxial cable
correctAnswer: It resists electrical noise, moisture and lightning
explanation: Fiber transmits light rather than electrical signals, eliminating electrical interference, and its immunity to moisture and lightning made it the standard between buildings.
